segment.description: Boiling Fork Creek, a small Franklin County stream in the Sewanee/Cowan area draining to the Elk River system (GNIS 01269369, HUC 06030003). TWRA winter put-and-take rainbow trout water, stocked at Cowan City Park (Franklin County).
segment.boundaries: Entire creek per catalog hydroIdentity (GNIS 01269369, HUC 06030003); the stocking site is Cowan City Park on the creek in Cowan, Franklin County. Catalog seasonMonths: Dec/Jan/Feb.

coldSource.notes: Small warmwater-drainage creek in the Elk River HUC; no cold-source mechanism documented in any source consulted. Its cold season is simply winter (TDEC grabs 9.76-13.82 deg C in Dec-Mar, below).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. Program design is winter put-and-take only (catalog seasonMonths Dec/Jan/Feb; TWRA workbook rows for the site are Winter-type). TDEC's own grabs show the creek at 27.7-31 deg C across June-September in 2017/2022/2023 - lethally warm for stocked rainbows - consistent with the Trout Management Plan statement that hatchery-supported streams are 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented; the creek is outside TWRA's wild trout waters and sits in a warmwater Elk River drainage.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grab samples put the creek at 29-31 deg C in summer 2017/2022/2023 and TWRA stocks it as a Winter-only rainbow put-and-take site (Cowan City Park), so trout cannot live through the warm season here.
